purpose: Replace the main hero with a happy driver using hand controls. Move the accepted crouching engineer into the middle small tile labelled Professional fitting and remove the rejected key-handover image.
mode: AI-generated campaign photograph using the real Jeff Gosling push-pull controls photograph as the hardware reference.
prompt:
Create one new premium, photorealistic website hero photograph for Mobility Station, a UK vehicle adaptation specialist. Use the supplied REAL Jeff Gosling push-pull hand-control product photograph as the strict hardware reference. This is a new customer scene, not an engineer scene or a key handover.

SCENE AND CAMERA: A naturally happy woman around 55–65 sits properly in the RIGHT-HAND driver's seat of this modern BMW, wearing a neat soft blue cardigan over a white top, seat belt correctly fastened from her right shoulder to her left hip. She is comfortably upright, looking forwards through the windscreen with a relaxed, visible smile as if enjoying her independence and ready to drive. The car is stationary in a pleasant leafy setting in daylight. Photograph from INSIDE the car, from the front passenger/centre area just behind her left shoulder, a convincing three-quarter side/over-shoulder view. Her smiling side profile is clearly visible in the right half, the actual steering wheel and hand control are clearly readable across the left/centre. Do not turn her head unnaturally toward the camera. The windshield, dashboard, front pillar, CLOSED driver's door with its window, interior door card and armrest, and driver seat all have coherent physical geometry. No open doorway, no cutaway car, nobody outside. Include enough of the intact cabin to make everything make sense. Single person only.

CRITICAL REAL PRODUCT FIDELITY: Reproduce the supplied real Jeff Gosling push-pull hand controls, preserving the recognisable grey textured cylindrical grip with its flared base, on its single black bent operating lever below and to the driver's RIGHT of the steering wheel, as in the photo. Preserve its proportions, mounting position and relationship to the wheel as faithfully as possible. This device is the one low-mounted adaptation grip, NOT the factory indicator/wiper stalk behind the upper-right wheel spoke. Keep the supplied BMW wheel, dashboard and normal factory stalks consistent. The woman's LEFT hand rests naturally on the left/top of the steering wheel. Her RIGHT hand rests naturally on the real low-mounted push-pull grip, with enough grey textured grip and black lever remaining visible to recognise it. Real anatomy: two arms, two hands, normal fingers; no hands passing through the rim or other parts. Never invent a second adaptation, steering ring, joystick, extra rods, unattached lever, dashboard-mounted gadget, floating mechanism or new technical hardware. The authentic referenced push-pull mechanism is the only driving adaptation shown. Her posture and reach must be plausible.

VISUAL STYLE: Genuine-looking high-end editorial automotive lifestyle photography, warm but restrained expression, natural skin and fabric detail, soft directional daylight, carefully exposed dark interior so the real controls remain visible, subtle navy/blue and neutral colours. An inviting happy-customer image, neither stock-photo exaggeration nor cinematic fantasy. Good detail on control, natural depth of field but no blur hiding the hardware. No captions, banners, text overlays, added logos, key handover, engineer or collage. Landscape 16:9 composition for the main hero, approximately 1792 by 1008. Leave a little breathing room around the woman's head and all important hardware so nothing essential is cut off.
review: The customer is seated and belted, smiling towards the windscreen. Left hand is on the wheel and right hand is on the grey push-pull grip below and to the right of the wheel. The grip and black lever resemble the supplied real product reference. A closed driver's door, door card, window, mirror and connected cabin are visible. This is generated imagery informed by a real reference; it is not unaltered product photography or a documentary photo of a real customer.

revision.reason: The customer identified the initial grip orientation and hand position as incorrect, and requested an upwards-pointing lever with fingers pulling it.
revision.prompt:
Make a tightly localised correction to IMAGE 1, the landscape photograph of the smiling woman driving. IMAGE 2 is the REAL Jeff Gosling push-pull hand-control reference. Preserve the woman, face, smile, gaze, seat belt, left arm on the steering wheel, blue clothing, dashboard, steering wheel, camera, closed door, mirror, outdoor background, lighting and full 16:9 composition from IMAGE 1. Only edit the adaptation lever/grip and the woman's RIGHT hand and wrist that operate it.

The customer has identified the control orientation and operation as wrong. Correct them visibly:
- The push-pull control's operating grip must point UPWARDS. Set the real grey textured cylindrical grip clearly upright, almost vertical with only a slight natural tilt, rising from the black bent lever beside the LOWER RIGHT of the steering wheel. Its top must be visibly higher than its base and visible ABOVE her gripping fingers. Do not leave the grip tilted forwards/down or looking like a horizontal handle.
- Match the actual grey Jeff Gosling grip shape, textured dots, proportions, flared base and SINGLE black bent push-pull lever shown in reference IMAGE 2. Keep the real lever's connection under the steering column physically coherent. Use this referenced adaptation, with no invented hardware.
- Move her RIGHT hand from resting over/capping the top to properly holding the SIDE of the UPRIGHT grip. Her four fingers are naturally curled around the front/far side of the handle in a PULLING action towards her body, with the thumb opposing them. Her wrist and palm sit at the middle/lower part of the upright handle rather than over its top. Leave the upper portion and top end of the grip clearly visible above her fingers so its UPWARD orientation is unmistakable. Natural slightly flexed pulling fingers, relaxed plausible wrist, one right hand with five anatomically correct digits.
- The hand must connect naturally to her existing right forearm; minimally adjust the wrist/forearm if necessary. It must read as gently PULLING the upright hand-control lever back towards herself, not pressing down on it, not gripping a gearstick, and not touching the factory stalk.
- No extra stalk, extra ring, joystick, duplicate handle, invented rod or disconnected mechanism. Do not modify the car body, door, woman's face or the rest of the approved photograph.

Photorealistic seamless edit, preserving the existing composition and colour. Do not add any text, diagram or explanation to the image. Output the entire corrected landscape photograph.
revision.review: The revised grip points upwards, with its top visible above the right hand and fingers wrapped around its side in a pulling position. The woman, her left hand, closed door and original composition remain visually consistent. The real Jeff Gosling photo was supplied again as reference. The generated hardware has not been independently validated as an exact technical representation.
